title: Pathology: inflammatory bowel disease — Crohn's disease or ulcerative colitis?

guidelineVersions: BSG colorectal surveillance in IBD (East et al., Gut 2025)

brief.scenario: A 28-year-old woman has a 3-month history of bloody diarrhoea, urgency and crampy abdominal pain. She has lost 4 kg. The examiner will show you her colonoscopy report, then her biopsy report.
brief.task: Interpret the reports, and compare the pathology of Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis.

beforeYouWalkIn.frame: Read the data first. Then compare: distribution, depth, histology, beyond the gut, cancer risk.
beforeYouWalkIn.trap: Reciting a comparison table without committing to what her reports show.
beforeYouWalkIn.firstMove: "This is continuous inflammation from the rectum with a normal ileum."

grid.label: Reads the colonoscopy
grid.fail: Calls it Crohn's disease, or ignores the normal ileum.
grid.pass: Continuous inflammation from the rectum to the splenic flexure, normal ileum: left-sided ulcerative colitis pattern.
grid.high: Says infection must still be excluded with stool culture and C. difficile testing.

grid.label: Distribution
grid.fail: Says both are confined to the colon.
grid.pass: Crohn's: anywhere from mouth to anus, skip lesions, often terminal ileum. UC: rectum, then continuous proximally, colon only.
grid.high: Names UC extent classes (proctitis, left-sided, extensive) and backwash ileitis in extensive colitis.

grid.label: Depth and complications
grid.pass: Crohn's is transmural; UC is mucosal.
grid.high: Links depth to complications: Crohn's fistulae, strictures and abscesses; UC pseudopolyps and toxic megacolon.

grid.label: Reads the biopsy
grid.fail: Cannot name a histological feature that separates them.
grid.pass: UC: crypt abscesses, goblet cell depletion, diffuse crypt distortion. Crohn's: non-caseating granulomas, transmural lymphoid aggregates, fissuring ulcers.
grid.high: Crypt distortion and basal plasmacytosis mean chronic IBD, not infection; absent granulomas do not exclude Crohn's.

grid.label: Beyond the gut
grid.pass: Peripheral and axial arthritis, erythema nodosum, pyoderma gangrenosum, episcleritis, uveitis, primary sclerosing cholangitis (mostly with UC).
grid.high: Erythema nodosum settles when the gut is controlled; axial arthritis and PSC can run their own course.

grid.label: Cancer risk and surveillance
grid.fail: Says IBD carries no cancer risk.
grid.pass: Colitis raises colorectal cancer risk: surveillance colonoscopy from 8 years after symptom onset; from diagnosis if PSC.
grid.high: Interval set by risk (annual for PSC, dysplasia, stricture, moderate inflammation); dye-spray chromoendoscopy with targeted biopsies; proctitis alone not surveyed.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: How does the distribution differ between Crohn's and UC?

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: They both affect the colon, so it's hard to tell.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: It shows inflammation, which confirms IBD.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: No, IBD isn't a cancer risk.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: There's continuous inflammation from the rectum to the splenic flexure, and the ileum is normal. That's a left-sided ulcerative colitis pattern.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Crohn's can affect anywhere from mouth to anus, with skip lesions, often the terminal ileum. UC starts in the rectum and extends continuously proximally, and stays in the colon.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Crohn's is transmural. UC is mucosal.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Crypt abscesses, goblet cell depletion and diffuse crypt distortion, confined to the mucosa, with no granulomas. That fits UC. In Crohn's I'd expect non-caseating granulomas, transmural lymphoid aggregates and fissuring ulcers.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Arthritis, peripheral and axial, erythema nodosum, pyoderma gangrenosum, episcleritis and uveitis, and primary sclerosing cholangitis, mostly with UC.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Colitis increases colorectal cancer risk. She'd be offered surveillance colonoscopy from 8 years after her symptoms started, or from diagnosis if she had PSC.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: It looks like left-sided UC, but I'd exclude infection first with stool culture and C. difficile testing.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: UC is described by extent: proctitis, left-sided or extensive. In extensive colitis you can get backwash ileitis, which isn't Crohn's.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Why does depth matter to a surgeon?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Transmural Crohn's causes fistulae, strictures and abscesses. Mucosal UC gives pseudopolyps and, in acute severe colitis, toxic megacolon.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: What tells you this is chronic, not infective?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Crypt distortion and basal plasmacytosis. And no granulomas doesn't exclude Crohn's, because biopsies often miss them.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Do those manifestations follow the gut?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Erythema nodosum usually settles when the gut is controlled. Axial arthritis and PSC can run their own course.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: The interval is set by risk. Annual if she has PSC, previous dysplasia, a stricture or moderate inflammation. Dye-spray chromoendoscopy with targeted biopsies. Proctitis alone isn't surveyed.

failures.move: Calling continuous rectal disease with a normal ileum Crohn's.
failures.consequence: Misreads the data the station is built on.

failures.move: Not naming granulomas or crypt distortion.
failures.consequence: Cannot separate Crohn's, UC and infection on histology.

failures.move: Not knowing IBD needs cancer surveillance.
failures.consequence: Misses when to start and who needs it sooner.

recovery.when: You're not sure which it is
recovery.line: Let me go by distribution, depth and histology in turn.
The pattern fits UC; I'd exclude infection before confirming it.

knowledge.fact: Crohn's: skip lesions, transmural, granulomas. UC: continuous from rectum, mucosal, crypt abscesses.
Crypt distortion and basal plasmacytosis indicate chronic IBD rather than infection.
Toxic megacolon: acute severe colitis with colonic dilatation over 6 cm.
Surveillance from 8 years after symptom onset; from diagnosis with PSC, then annually.
Isolated proctitis and terminal ileal Crohn's do not need colonoscopic surveillance.

recall.think: Distribution, depth, histology. Then cancer risk.
recall.say: "Continuous from the rectum, normal ileum, mucosal: ulcerative colitis."
recall.trap: No granulomas does not exclude Crohn's.
recall.finish: Exclude infection; plan surveillance by risk.

sources.name: East JE, et al. British Society of Gastroenterology guidelines on colorectal surveillance in inflammatory bowel disease. Gut 2025 (doi:10.1136/gutjnl-2025-335023)
sources.supports: Start of surveillance 8 years after symptom onset; PSC from diagnosis and annually; risk-based intervals; dye-based chromoendoscopy; exclusion of proctitis and ileal Crohn's

media.task: Describe the histology and say which disease it favours
media.description: Paired biopsy images: UC (crypt abscess, goblet cell depletion, crypt distortion) and Crohn's (non-caseating granuloma)

partner.opening: Here is her colonoscopy report. Tell me what it shows.

reveals.finding: Colonoscopy: continuous erythema, loss of vascular pattern and contact bleeding from the rectum to the splenic flexure. Normal mucosa beyond. Terminal ileum normal.
Biopsies: diffuse crypt distortion, basal plasmacytosis, crypt abscesses and goblet cell depletion, confined to the mucosa. No granulomas.
Stool culture and C. difficile toxin negative.

push.question: How does the distribution differ?
push.expect: Crohn's anywhere, skip lesions, terminal ileum. UC rectum then continuous, colon only.

push.question: How does depth affect complications?
push.expect: Transmural: fistulae, strictures, abscesses. Mucosal: pseudopolyps, toxic megacolon.

push.question: What is toxic megacolon?
push.expect: Acute severe colitis with colonic dilatation over 6 cm and systemic toxicity; risk of perforation.

push.question: When does surveillance start?
push.expect: 8 years after symptom onset; from diagnosis with PSC, annually.

curveballs.prompt: She develops a perianal fistula. Does that change your view?
curveballs.safeAnswer: It suggests Crohn's disease, because transmural inflammation forms fistulae. Review the whole bowel.

curveballs.prompt: Her ALP is raised. What do you worry about?
curveballs.safeAnswer: Primary sclerosing cholangitis: MRCP, and colonoscopic surveillance from diagnosis, annually.
